reviews.evidence: Shipped LAN and optional remote mobile access preserve DSH sessions and tools; the README walks through independent LAN/remote pairing and /mobile customization, with screenshots of access panels and two customized interfaces plus explicit compatibility, security, upgrade, purge, and fail-closed version checks.
reviews.concern: Remote access depends on third-party tunnel limits and currently narrows managed remote support to Windows x64; paired devices receive full DSH control.

reviews.evidence: Provides relay- and project-attributed usage, balance and subscription windows, pricing, drill-down analysis, export, diagnostics, reindexing, declared endpoints, API/library access, and detailed commands; correctness tests, explicit accounting rules, endpoint safeguards, recovery behavior, and provider edge cases are concrete.
reviews.concern: Only one explicitly demo-data panel screenshot is visible, so the unusually broad operational surface is documented much more strongly than it is visually demonstrated.

reviews.evidence: Ships exact multi-frame previews, read-only inspection, managed editing, direct-canvas tools, and a private-draft-to-atomic-publish pipeline with a detailed production workflow, tool reference, build verification, platform matrix, recovery drafts, conflict handling, quality gates, and current limits.
reviews.concern: The README shows one main overview image rather than representative before/after artifacts for the many pipeline stages, and its explicit task scenarios are narrower than its technical reference.

reviews.evidence: Covers runtime injection, automatic and self reload, staging/promotion, uninstall, route cleanup, persistence, status checks, scaffolding, building, release packaging, and a daemon example; it also documents install/develop/uninstall workflows, rollback, stress tests, compatibility, recovery, and concrete failure pitfalls.
reviews.concern: The README supplies extensive claims, commands, and test summaries but no screenshot, captured tool result, or other rich shipped-output demonstration.

reviews.evidence: Its own marketplace workflow includes scheduled registry construction, fallback discovery, search/category browsing, four-type detection, guarded installation, installed/version recognition, updates, skills browsing, uninstall, feedback, backup/restore, and documented HTTP states; security controls, cleanup behavior, fallbacks, and known limits are explicit.
reviews.concern: The visible image is a social preview rather than a product-state demonstration, and catalog inclusion/classification is explicitly not verification or endorsement of listed projects.

reviews.evidence: Shows a shipped desktop agent with Galgame presentation, voice/BGM, nine provider presets, setup diagnostics, character editing, uploads, commands, saves, and updating; multiple screenshots cover chat, setup, provider selection, character editing, and settings, and the README states cache/upload bounds and content/cost caveats.
reviews.concern: Beyond installation and API configuration, the README gives no followable operational happy path for using the agent's features; testing, troubleshooting, and failure behavior are also largely absent.

reviews.evidence: Ships a broad collection of completed infrastructure and visualization skills, with concrete request/output examples for GPU kernels, memory estimation, RL setup, flowcharts, and slides, plus multiple real diagram/PDF artifacts and pytest commands alongside stated quality criteria.
reviews.concern: The repository warns that it is heavily LLM-generated without strict proofreading and requires production verification; the README provides test procedures but no test results for the whole collection.

reviews.evidence: Combines the official DSH UI with a launcher, Git actions, files/diff/browser/agents surfaces, terminal, model and vision controls, appearance, extension management, updates, crash restart, and plugin recovery; screenshots show several surfaces, while compatibility, migration, checksum, tests, fail-closed resources, and production acceptance boundaries are concrete.
reviews.concern: Most feature use is stated rather than walked through; the clearest complete operational flow is upgrade-data recovery, while launcher and plugin-recovery behavior receive little direct demonstration.

reviews.evidence: Documents an end-to-end macOS flow from permission checks and action recording through inspection, validation, structured session/event artifacts, skill-input packaging, and agent handoff; it includes a worked file-sending demonstration, several explicit UI-workflow scenarios, CLI reference, output trees, privacy boundaries, requirements, and stable-scope limits.
reviews.concern: It is explicitly alpha and macOS-only, captures no screenshots in the core path, and delegates final skill creation to the consuming agent rather than shipping that outcome itself.

reviews.evidence: Ships a bounded five-part session handoff with preview/edit, clean-target migration, wait/continue choices, image-policy branches, native-card and text fallbacks, doctor checks, and rollback to the untouched source; commands, decision tables, a real migration GIF, regression results, compatibility gates, 160-test verification, fail-closed behavior, and limits are all concrete.
reviews.concern: The product deliberately solves one bounded migration problem, and its native-card repeat evidence is only three fixed runs rather than a statistical guarantee.
